purpose: R113 physical-router HELLO/PING held-connection memory screen; prepare ten frozen serial windows, no installation or performance adoption.
candidate_source: R112 boxed-client experiment plus R113 prefix/body-bounded FD receive correction; accepted root runtime remains unchanged.
sampling: Each window starts a fresh daemon for each connection count. Save one validated status snapshot per before/held/after-disconnect phase, bracket it by PID/starttime checks, and derive CSV from that same snapshot. Pin every subject to CPU1 with identical argv[0].
readiness: Exact HELLO and PING DATA/STATUS validation for every held connection; daemon FD count must grow by N and return to baseline. Invalid status, absent fields, changed identity or unexpected exit rejects the window.
retention_rule: Candidate RssAnon growth at 64 held connections must be <=38.4 KiB in both blocks. This fixed screen does not establish runtime adoption; retain and report failing measurements too.
analysis: Report both blocks, paired differences, all absolute VmRSS/RssAnon/VmData, held growth, after-disconnect values and retained growth for all five subjects. Do not pool earlier runs; no CPU, FD-workload, whole-memory superiority or equivalence claim.
pss: This exact router lacks smaps/smaps_rollup: PSS remains NA, never zero. Process RSS does not measure kernel socket buffers, peaks or removable system RAM.
known_control_defect: R109 (before) and R112 have verified SCM_RIGHTS/frame-boundary defects. They remain explicitly labeled historical memory controls; this workload sends validated HELLO/PING only and no FDs. Their memory values do not establish FD compatibility or FD performance.

oracle_gates.validation: Require the frozen completed report SHA, final passed=true, finished, exactly six required exit-zero results, matching candidate ELF and validator SHA. Require all prerequisite evidence unchanged before and after every window.

failure_rule: No device command until both frozen preflights and all Oracle gates pass. Verify every ELF/helper/script/guard/recovery hash before and after each window, plus result health/boot/config/production/mount identity and cleanup. Stop on any failure; retain failed window and FAILED.json; never skip, resume into an existing root, or substitute artifacts.
production: Stock C throughout, guarded disposable mount/PID/net namespaces and no installation. Driver verifies the separate recovery gate and management-client health for every window.
completion: After all ten windows validate, run tools/r105_rx_spare_report.py and emit report.json plus memory-gate.json. A failed memory threshold preserves a complete collection and a false gate result; it is not a collection failure.
